Gaming · Player culture

You do not have to finish your backlog

Make space for play without turning it into a second job.

By The Offbeat Edit · Culture Issue · 1 min read

Separate interest from obligation

A library is a collection of possibilities, not a list of debts. Notice which games you want to return to and which ones you only feel guilty about leaving unfinished.

Choose one game that suits your time and mood now. A title you bought for a different season of life does not need to be today’s priority.

Give yourself a smaller goal

Try one level, one evening, or the tutorial. A limited visit lets you decide whether a game is a good fit without promising to reach the credits.

If you return after a long break, check for a recap, revisit the controls, or start a separate save if the game supports it. Protect an existing save before making changes.

Let stopping be a choice

You can appreciate a game’s ideas without completing every challenge. If the experience is no longer enjoyable, leaving it is a reasonable outcome.

Keep a short note about where you stopped only if you might return. The point is to make coming back easier, not to create another tracking system you must maintain.

Make space for play without turning it into a second job.
